description:
Saves the Dynamic DNS settings; send only what changes. Fields set by environment variables are ignored. A time must be from 1m to 24h. A service must be an https:// URL, 1 to 10 of them; a literal address the server may not call is refused with 400, and so is a name that resolves to one (error.ddns-service-blocked). A change of the period restarts the timer. Nothing is reloaded.

Needs: an administrator (a token needs its Administrator switch)

requestBody.description: The settings to change; fields you leave out keep their value

period.description: How often the dynamic DNS records are checked, a time from 1m to 24h such as 5m or 1h30m (env DDNS_PERIOD); a change restarts the timer

cooldown.description: The shortest time between two changes of one record, a time from 1m to 24h (env DDNS_COOLDOWN)

ipv4_services.description: The services asked for the instance's public IPv4 address, https:// URLs; a new list needs at least 2, since a new address counts only when a second service confirms it (a stored list of one is kept while a save leaves it unchanged); a literal address the server may not call, or a name that resolves to one, is refused (env DDNS_IPV4_SERVICES)

ipv6_services.description: The services asked for the instance's public IPv6 address, https:// URLs; a new list needs at least 2, since a new address counts only when a second service confirms it (a stored list of one is kept while a save leaves it unchanged); a literal address the server may not call, or a name that resolves to one, is refused (env DDNS_IPV6_SERVICES)

resolver.description: DNS servers the updater asks for a record's current address, IPv4 addresses or IPv6 addresses in brackets with an optional :port; empty uses the container's own resolvers (env DDNS_RESOLVER)

200.description: The Dynamic DNS settings after the save, in the same form as the GET answer
